title: The party's "insurgents" keep showing up with billionaires behind them
body: The Lever spent this week tracing where the Democratic establishment's money actually goes. In Connecticut, Luke Bronin toppled 14-term Rep. John Larson and sold it as generational change. Behind that "insurgent" win, The Lever found Stephen Mandel, a 70-year-old hedge fund billionaire who founded Lone Pine Capital and has become the party's new kingmaker. The Mandels have given roughly $84 million to Democrats over the years. Their latest $15 million is bankrolling two new outfits, Majority Democrats and the Bench, built to hand establishment candidates the machinery to beat progressives.

The money is not always this quiet. The Lever also reports that Third Way, the corporate-funded centrist group, is spending its own $15 million to discredit the Democratic Socialists of America, which it calls a "mortal danger." That funding traces back to health insurers, the same industry that has fought Medicare for All for years. One wing of the party quietly buys primaries. The other openly declares war on its own voters.

It is not working cleanly. Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate primary over the establishment's pick despite about $65 million in outside money against him. Francesca Hong lost Wisconsin's governor race by four-tenths of a point. The lesson keeps going unlearned. Spend a fortune to crush a movement and you mostly prove it was worth joining.
